# storage/cache

Cache used by the risk and strategy layers for values that are expensive to recompute on every
tick. `api()` stays in-memory, single-process, no external backend — cheap-to-recompute derived
data with no restart-survival requirement. `rolling_state()`, as of trading-platform#79, is backed
by a durable Postgres-backed store in production so per-algo strategy state survives a process
restart within the same trading session (see below).

## Files

**`base.py`** — `KVCache` protocol (structural: async `get`/`set`/`delete`). Both `ValueCache` and
`PostgresKVCache` satisfy it without inheriting from it. `BaseCacher.__init__` takes a `KVCache`.

**`backend.py`** — `ValueCache` — in-memory dict with per-key TTL. Still backs `api()`, and backs
`rolling_state()` too in any test/dev wiring that doesn't pass a durable `rolling_state_cache`.

**`postgres_backend.py`** — `PostgresKVCache` — durable `KVCache` implementation backed by the
`rolling_state_cache` Postgres table (`storage/cache/models.py`), using
`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` for `set()`. Has no TTL/expiry mechanism — `set(ttl=...)` logs a
warning and ignores it. Production wiring (`di/containers/infra.py`) injects this into
`CacherFactory` as `rolling_state_cache` so `rolling_state()` state survives a restart; `api()`
keeps using the shared in-memory `cache`.

**`factory.py`** — `CacherFactory` — the single injectable object. Vends named cache instances:
- `factory.rolling_state()` — per-algo rolling state (indicator warm-up data), backed by
  `rolling_state_cache` if given, else falls back to the shared `cache`.
- `factory.api()` — always backed by the shared `cache`.

Daily realized PnL is no longer cached here — a process-local cache silently diverged across
concurrent worker processes (see `execution/storage/store.py`'s `TradingStore`, which now owns
`increment_pnl_aggregate`/`get_pnl_aggregate` backed by a `strategy_aggregates` Postgres table
updated via `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).

**`rolling_state.py`** — `RollingStateCacher` — saves/loads per-algo-symbol-interval state
snapshots (JSON-encoded), backed by any `KVCache`. `save()` takes a required `saved_at` timestamp;
`load_latest()` takes a required `now` and refuses to return state saved on a different calendar
day than `now`, or with no recorded save timestamp at all (a pre-#79 cache row) — both are treated
as stale and fall back to warmup, on the principle that restoring cross-day-stale intraday
indicator state could be worse than a clean reseed. Used by `SignalGenerator.restore_state()`,
called after `setup()`'s warmup replay and after `rewarm_after_login()`'s per-symbol re-warm, so a
valid restored entry overrides the just-seeded warmup state rather than the other way around.

**`api.py`** — `ApiResponseCacher` — caches HTTP API responses (e.g. instrument list), backed by
the shared `ValueCache`.

**`models.py`** — `RollingStateCacheRow` ORM model for the `rolling_state_cache` table, under its
own `Base`. This is a deliberate 9th competing per-module `Base`/metadata object on top of the 8
that trading-platform#35 flags as a schema-drift risk — done specifically so
`app.database.init_db()`'s per-Base `create_all()` sweep creates this table automatically for
every SQLite-backed unit test, matching this codebase's existing test-infra convention. Argued not
to carry #35's actual risk: no duplicate/competing model for this table, no relationships, and a
hand-written (not autogenerated) migration.

## Setup

```python
from trading.storage.cache import CacherFactory, ValueCache
from trading.storage.cache.postgres_backend import PostgresKVCache

# In-memory only (tests, or rolling_state() without restart-survival):
factory = CacherFactory(ValueCache(), clock)

# Production: rolling_state() durable, api() still in-memory.
factory = CacherFactory(ValueCache(), clock, rolling_state_cache=PostgresKVCache(session_factory))
```
